concepts.title: Decimals: Beyond the Point, Again
concepts.definition: A second peek beyond the point extends the story to longer decimals: place values continue through tenths, hundredths and thousandths, and everyday measures like 2.75 litres get exact decimal homes.
concepts.key_idea: The point opens an endless street of places: each step right divides by ten again.
concepts.textbook_ref: gegp204.txt, Another Peek Beyond the Point

concepts.title: Multiplying Decimals by Powers of Ten
concepts.definition: Multiplying a decimal by 10, 100 or 1000 simply shifts the point one, two or three places to the right, because each shift multiplies every place value by ten.
concepts.key_idea: Powers of ten move the point without touching the digits: the digits stay, the point travels.

solution_steps.explain: Each power of ten shifts the point one more place to the right.
Move the point by as many places as the power of ten.

concepts.title: Adding and Subtracting Decimals
concepts.definition: Decimal sums and differences are safe when the points are aligned: tenths fall under tenths and hundredths under hundredths, and empty places are filled with zeros before adding or subtracting.
concepts.key_idea: Aligned points align places: once columns match, decimal addition is ordinary column addition.
concepts.textbook_ref: gegp204.txt, Addition and subtraction of decimals

subtract 3.8 from 9.2

solution_steps.explain: Write both numbers with points in one column, filling zeros where needed.
Add place by place from the right; the point stays in its column.

concepts.title: Comparing and Ordering Decimals
concepts.definition: Decimals are compared place by place from the left: equal whole parts are decided by tenths, then hundredths, and trailing zeros like 4.50 and 4.5 name the same number.
concepts.key_idea: Longer is not bigger: a decimal with more digits may still be smaller, so places decide, not lengths.
